subject.title: [Feature]: First-class multi-instance management for Docker installs

question: Should OpenClaw core own first-class Docker instance create/list/delete/update commands, or should multi-instance Docker operation remain documented manual Compose/profile usage or live in an external helper/plugin?
rationale: The current product has enough primitives to run multiple gateways manually, but adding official instance lifecycle creates new persistent state, deletion/update, security, and setup UX contracts that require maintainer product direction.

options.title: Approve a minimal core lifecycle
options.body: Design a narrow core-owned instance command set with explicit persistence, port, Compose project, update/delete, doctor, and sandbox semantics before implementation.

options.title: Keep manual profile and Compose operation
options.body: Close or defer the feature and improve docs around profiles, env vars, ClawDock, and known multi-instance hazards instead of adding a new command surface.

options.title: Route to external helper or plugin
options.body: Let a maintained ClawDock-style helper own orchestration while core only adds missing APIs if the helper cannot express a safe workflow.

recommendation.title: Approve a minimal core lifecycle
recommendation.body: Design a narrow core-owned instance command set with explicit persistence, port, Compose project, update/delete, doctor, and sandbox semantics before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans CLI profile/service naming and multi-gateway docs where this history shows the strongest recent ownership signal.
